cases.n: Ferns Report — Diocese of Ferns
cases.victims_note: More than 100 allegations made between 1962 and 2002
cases.who: Catholic Diocese of Ferns
cases.cover: Bishop Herlihy moved accused priests to other posts or dioceses for a period, then reinstated them; Gardaí failed to record or properly investigate some pre-1988 complaints
cases.d: The state Ferns Inquiry, published 25 October 2005, examined more than 100 allegations of child sexual abuse made between 1962 and 2002 against 21 priests of the diocese. Bishop Donal Herlihy moved accused priests temporarily and then reinstated them, and ordained men he knew or should have known posed a risk. Bishop Brendan Comiskey never got a priest to stand aside from ministry. The report found Garda handling of one of eight formal complaints 'wholly inadequate' and some pre-1988 complaints were not recorded.
cases.cite: Ferns Inquiry report, 25 October 2005, as reported by RTÉ News

cases.n: Murphy Report — Archdiocese of Dublin
cases.victims_note: 320 people complained of abuse 1975–2004; a further 130 complaints after May 2004
cases.who: Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin
cases.cover: Abuse 'covered up' 1975–2004; bishops generally did not report to Gardaí before 1996; archdiocese took out insurance against abuse litigation from 1987; Gardaí knew of complaints against Fr Tony Walsh in 1990–91 and took no action
cases.d: The Commission of Investigation into the Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin reported on 26 November 2009. It examined a sample of 46 priests out of 102 within its remit; 320 people complained of abuse between 1975 and 2004. It found Archbishops McQuaid, Ryan, McNamara and Connell handled complaints badly and that the archdiocese had insured itself against abuse litigation from 1987. It also criticised the Gardaí, and the Garda Commissioner apologised.
cases.cite: Commission of Investigation, Report into the Catholic Archdiocese of Dublin (Murphy Report), 26 November 2009

cases.n: Cloyne Report — Diocese of Cloyne
cases.who: Catholic Diocese of Cloyne; Bishop John Magee
cases.cover: Nine complaints that should have gone to the Gardaí were not reported; none of the 1996–2008 complaints reported to the health service; Vatican's reaction to Irish guidelines described as 'entirely unhelpful'
cases.d: The Cloyne Report, published 13 July 2011, examined the diocese's handling of allegations against 19 clerics from 1996 to February 2009, after the Irish church had adopted reporting procedures. Nine complaints that should have been reported to the Gardaí were not, and none were reported to the health authorities. Bishop John Magee was found to have shown little interest in applying the guidelines for 12 years. The report said the Vatican's response to the Irish procedures allowed bishops to ignore them.
cases.cite: Commission of Investigation, Report into the Catholic Diocese of Cloyne, July 2011, as summarised by the Irish Times

cases.n: Ryan Commission — industrial schools run by religious orders
cases.victims_note: More than 30,000 children were sent to the institutions; redress scheme paid about 12,000 people
cases.who: Christian Brothers (most boys' institutions), Sisters of Mercy (most girls' institutions) and other Catholic orders
cases.cover: Christian Brothers sued the commission in 2004 to keep members' names out; no real names of perpetrators published; findings not to be used for prosecutions; state Department of Education inspections failed
cases.d: The Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse reported on 20 May 2009 after a nine-year investigation of more than 250 church-run institutions that held over 30,000 children from the 1930s to the 1990s. It found sexual abuse 'endemic' in boys' institutions run mainly by the Christian Brothers; the Sisters of Mercy ran most girls' institutions. The 2,600-page report names no perpetrators after a Christian Brothers lawsuit. A parallel state redress scheme paid about 12,000 people an average of €65,000.
cases.cite: Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse (Ryan Report), 20 May 2009, as reported by CBS News/AP

cases.n: Scoping Inquiry — abuse in religious-run schools
cases.victims_note: 2,395 allegations recorded; report says true number likely higher
cases.who: 42 religious orders that ran day and boarding schools
cases.d: The state Scoping Inquiry, published 3 September 2024, recorded 2,395 allegations of sexual abuse against 884 alleged abusers at 308 schools run by 42 religious orders, mostly from the 1960s to the 1990s. 590 allegations involving 190 alleged abusers concerned 17 special schools. More than half of the alleged abusers are dead. The government announced a full Commission of Investigation.
cases.cite: Report of the Scoping Inquiry into Historical Sexual Abuse in Day and Boarding Schools Run by Religious Orders, 3 September 2024

cases.n: Archdiocese of Boston — Spotlight 2002 and Massachusetts AG report 2003
cases.victims_note: At least 789 minors; AG estimated the true number probably exceeds 1,000
cases.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston; Cardinal Bernard Law
cases.cover: Accused priests reassigned with Cardinal Law's personal involvement; church alerted law enforcement only twice in six decades; bishops sought leniency for priests and withheld information from prosecutors
cases.d: After the Boston Globe Spotlight series beginning January 2002, Cardinal Law resigned in December 2002. The Massachusetts Attorney General's report of 23 July 2003 found at least 237 priests and 13 other church workers accused of abusing at least 789 minors over six decades, and 'overwhelming evidence' that Law knew and took part in reassigning abusers. No criminal statute allowed charging church leaders.
cases.cite: Office of the Massachusetts Attorney General, 'The Sexual Abuse of Children in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston', 23 July 2003, as reported by the Boston Globe

cases.n: Pennsylvania grand jury — six dioceses
cases.place: Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, Allentown, Scranton, Greensburg, Erie
cases.victims_note: 'At least 1,000' identified; grand jury believed there were more
cases.who: Six Pennsylvania Catholic dioceses
cases.cover: Abusers moved and protected, some later promoted; reports brushed aside; most crimes beyond statute of limitations
cases.d: A 23-member statewide grand jury report released by Attorney General Josh Shapiro on 14 August 2018 identified 301 'predator priests' and at least 1,000 child victims over about 70 years in six dioceses. The roughly 1,400-page report found bishops 'went to great lengths to keep it secret' and moved abusers. Most crimes were too old to prosecute.
cases.cite: 40th Statewide Investigating Grand Jury report, 14 August 2018, as reported by America magazine

cases.n: Illinois Attorney General — clergy abuse report
cases.who: Six Catholic dioceses of Illinois
cases.cover: Before the investigation the dioceses had publicly listed only 103 substantiated abusers
cases.d: Attorney General Kwame Raoul's report of 23 May 2023, from an investigation opened in 2018, named 451 Catholic clerics and religious brothers who abused at least 1,997 children in Illinois' six dioceses over decades. Before the inquiry the dioceses had publicly listed 103 substantiated abusers.
cases.cite: Illinois Attorney General, Report on Catholic Clergy Child Sex Abuse in Illinois, 23 May 2023

cases.n: John Jay College study — US Catholic clergy 1950–2002
cases.place: United States (commissioned by US bishops, Washington DC)
cases.victims_note: 10,667 individuals reported abuse to bishops; authors say true number likely higher
cases.who: US Conference of Catholic Bishops (commissioned study)
cases.cover: Of accused priests whose cases reached police, only one in three was charged; 3% served prison time
cases.d: The John Jay College of Criminal Justice study, commissioned by the US bishops and released 27 February 2004, counted 4,392 priests and deacons (about 4% of clergy) accused of abusing 10,667 minors between 1950 and 2002. Reported abuse peaked in the 1970s; one-third of allegations were made only in 2002–03. 149 priests with more than 10 allegations each accounted for 27% of allegations. Costs to the church were put at $472 million at the time.
cases.cite: John Jay College, 'The Nature and Scope of Sexual Abuse of Minors by Catholic Priests and Deacons in the United States 1950–2002', 2004, as summarised by America magazine

cases.n: Maryland Attorney General — Archdiocese of Baltimore
cases.victims_note: 'Over 600' children; report says true number 'likely far higher'
cases.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Baltimore
cases.cover: Archdiocese often failed to report to authorities or remove abusers; some accused allowed to retire with support; post-2002 public list omitted known abusers
cases.d: The Maryland Attorney General's report, released in redacted form on 5 April 2023, identified 156 priests and others associated with the Archdiocese of Baltimore who abused more than 600 children over 80 years. Attorney General Anthony Brown described 'repeated coverup' by the church. A judge ordered the names and titles of 37 people redacted.
cases.cite: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Report on Child Sexual Abuse in the Archdiocese of Baltimore, 5 April 2023, as reported by Fortune/AP

cases.n: Missouri Attorney General — four Catholic dioceses
cases.who: Archdiocese of St. Louis and dioceses of Kansas City–St. Joseph, Jefferson City, Springfield–Cape Girardeau
cases.d: Attorney General Eric Schmitt reported on 13 September 2019 on a review, opened in August 2018, of records of more than 2,000 priests who served in Missouri since 1945. It found 163 credible allegations of abuse or misconduct against minors by diocesan priests and deacons; 83 of the accused had died and the statute of limitations had expired for 46 alleged crimes. Twelve former priests were referred for prosecution.
cases.cite: Missouri Attorney General's Office, clergy abuse report, 13 September 2019, as reported by NPR/KPBS

cases.n: Michigan Attorney General — clergy abuse investigation
cases.victims_note: 552 victims identified by December 2019; AG expected 'several thousand' by the end
cases.who: Catholic dioceses of Michigan
cases.d: Attorney General Dana Nessel said on 23 December 2019 that the state investigation had identified 270 priests alleged to have abused 552 victims. Seven priests had been charged in 2019, two of whom had pleaded guilty. Most cases could not be prosecuted because of statutes of limitations.
cases.cite: Detroit News, 23 December 2019, reposted by BishopAccountability.org; Michigan AG press releases

cases.n: Archdiocese of Agaña — Archbishop Apuron and bankruptcy
cases.victims_note: More than 220 former altar boys, students and Boy Scouts sued
cases.who: Archdiocese of Agaña; former Archbishop Anthony Apuron
cases.d: A Vatican tribunal of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith found former Archbishop Anthony Apuron guilty of some charges including sexual abuse of minors in March 2018; the appeal was rejected in February 2019. He was barred from office and from living in Guam but not laicised; he denies the allegations. The archdiocese filed for bankruptcy in January 2019 facing more than 200 lawsuits naming 35 clergy, teachers and scoutmasters. Guam lifted the civil statute of limitations in 2016.
cases.cite: Catholic News Agency/EWTN News, 8 August 2019; America magazine, 9 November 2018

cases.n: Mount Cashel Orphanage — Hughes Royal Commission
cases.who: Congregation of Christian Brothers, Mount Cashel Orphanage
cases.cover: Inquiry found officials transferred offenders and covered up the abuse; insufficient evidence to charge church and government officials with obstruction
cases.d: The provincial Royal Commission led by Samuel Hughes (begun 1 June 1989, reported 1991–92) examined abuse of boys by Christian Brothers at Mount Cashel orphanage, which closed in 1990, and the justice system's response. It found officials had transferred offenders and covered up the abuse. Eleven Christian Brothers were convicted, with sentences from 4 months to 11 years. The Brothers apologised in April 1992; the Newfoundland government paid $11.5 million in 1996.
cases.cite: Royal Commission of Inquiry into the Response of the Newfoundland Criminal Justice System to Complaints (Hughes Inquiry), 1991–92

cases.n: Winter Commission — Archdiocese of St. John's
cases.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of St. John's; Archbishop Alphonsus Penney
cases.cover: Report assigned Archbishop Penney part of the blame for covering up abuse
cases.d: Archbishop Alphonsus Penney commissioned former Lieutenant Governor Gordon Winter in May 1989 to inquire into sexual abuse of children by clergy of the archdiocese. The 1990 report assigned Penney part of the blame for covering up abuse, and he resigned after its release.
cases.cite: Report of the Archdiocesan Commission of Enquiry into the Sexual Abuse of Children by Members of the Clergy (Winter Report), 1990

cases.n: Cornwall Public Inquiry
cases.who: Roman Catholic Diocese of Alexandria-Cornwall, local police and other institutions
cases.d: Ontario's Cornwall Public Inquiry, established 14 April 2005 under Commissioner G. Normand Glaude, examined how institutions including the Catholic diocese and local police responded to child sexual abuse allegations against adults in positions of trust, including Catholic clergy. Its 2009 report found systemic failures in the justice system's response. The commissioner declined to make a finding on whether a child-abuse ring existed, saying it was outside the mandate. The inquiry cost $53 million.
cases.cite: Report of the Cornwall Inquiry, December 2009

cases.n: Royal Commission — Catholic Church data, Australia
cases.victims_note: 4,444 people reported abuse at more than 1,000 Catholic institutions (claims 1980–2015)
cases.who: Catholic Church in Australia, incl. St John of God Brothers (40.4% of brothers accused)
cases.d: Data presented to the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse on 6 February 2017 showed 4,444 people reported abuse to Catholic authorities between 1980 and 2015, at more than 1,000 institutions, naming 1,880 alleged perpetrators. About 7% of priests who served between 1950 and 2010 were alleged perpetrators; 40.4% of St John of God Brothers were accused. Religious brothers (32%) and priests (30%) were the largest groups. The commission referred 309 cases to police.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Case Study 50 data, 6 February 2017, as reported by NPR

cases.n: Diocese of Ballarat — Gerald Ridsdale and Royal Commission Case Study 28
cases.victims_note: Convicted of abusing more than 70 children; advocates estimate hundreds
cases.who: Catholic Diocese of Ballarat; Bishop Ronald Mulkearns
cases.cover: Ridsdale moved through about 13 postings 1962–1991; Mulkearns knew by late 1975; a senior police officer in 1972 offered a detective promotion to stop investigating Monsignor John Day
cases.d: Gerald Ridsdale, ordained 1961, was convicted in a series of trials from 1993 of abusing more than 70 children; he died in prison in 2025. He was moved between parishes including Mildura, Swan Hill, Warrnambool, Apollo Bay, Edenhope and Mortlake, then to Sydney. The Royal Commission's Ballarat report of 6 December 2017 found Bishop Mulkearns knew of his offending by late 1975 and still reappointed him, a 'catastrophic' failure. It also found police obstruction of a 1972 investigation of Monsignor John Day.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Report of Case Study 28 (Ballarat), December 2017; The Courier (Ballarat)

cases.n: Cardinal George Pell — convicted 2018, acquitted 2020
cases.who: Cardinal George Pell (former Archbishop of Melbourne, Vatican treasurer)
cases.d: A Melbourne jury convicted Cardinal George Pell in December 2018 on five charges relating to two choirboys at St Patrick's Cathedral in 1996. On 7 April 2020 the High Court of Australia unanimously quashed the convictions and entered acquittals; he had served more than 400 days in prison. Separately, Royal Commission findings released in May 2020 said Pell was aware of abuse by clergy in the 1970s; he disputed this. He died in 2023.
cases.cite: Pell v The Queen [2020] HCA 12, 7 April 2020, as reported by 1News

cases.n: Royal Commission into Abuse in Care — Catholic institutions
cases.victims_note: About 200,000 abused across all state and faith-based care 1950–2019 (not Catholic alone); church data showed 14% of NZ clergy accused 1950–1999
cases.who: Catholic Church in Aotearoa New Zealand; St John of God Brothers at Marylands School
cases.cover: Church relied on psychiatrists' opinions to transfer abusers to other ministries where they reoffended; commission recommended investigating priests transferred to Papua New Guinea
cases.d: The Royal Commission's final report, Whanaketia, published 24 July 2024, found about 200,000 people were abused in state and faith-based care from 1950 to 2019. It found Catholic responses inadequate, noting a 2020 church briefing that 14% of clergy were accused over 1950–1999, and singled out Marylands School in Christchurch for some of the highest levels of sexual abuse. It found abusers were transferred to other ministries and recommended an inquiry into priests sent to Papua New Guinea.
cases.cite: Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care, Whanaketia, 24 July 2024, as reported by EWTN/CNA

cases.n: IICSA — Roman Catholic Church in England and Wales
cases.victims_note: More than 900 complaints involving over 3,000 instances of abuse, 1970–2015
cases.who: Catholic Church in England and Wales; Cardinal Vincent Nichols
cases.cover: Accused priests reassigned to other parishes; Holy See and Apostolic Nuncio refused to provide a witness statement
cases.d: The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse reported on 10 November 2020 that the Church in England and Wales received more than 900 complaints involving over 3,000 instances of child sexual abuse between 1970 and 2015, with more than 100 allegations a year since 2016. It found the church put its reputation before children and criticised Cardinal Nichols. The Holy See declined to provide a witness statement.
cases.cite: IICSA, The Roman Catholic Church: Safeguarding in the Roman Catholic Church in England and Wales, 10 November 2020

cases.n: IICSA — Ampleforth and Downside Benedictine schools
cases.who: English Benedictine Congregation — Ampleforth Abbey and Downside Abbey schools
cases.cover: Both institutions for decades avoided giving police and social services information; 'tell them nothing' approach after 2001
cases.d: The IICSA report of 9 August 2018 found a culture of acceptance of abuse at Ampleforth and Downside, where children as young as seven and eleven were abused over about four decades. Ten people linked to the schools, mostly monks, were convicted or cautioned for sexual or indecent-image offences. Both abbeys tried for decades to avoid passing information to police and social services.
cases.cite: IICSA, Ampleforth and Downside (English Benedictine Congregation case study), 9 August 2018; RTÉ

cases.n: IICSA — Archdiocese of Birmingham
cases.who: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Birmingham
cases.cover: Fr James Robinson moved parish after 1980s complaints, police not told; he fled to the US in 1985 and received archdiocesan payments for seven years; the Vicar General helped Fr Samuel Penney avoid arrest and leave the UK
cases.d: The IICSA case study report of 20 June 2019 found more than 130 allegations against 78 people associated with the archdiocese since the 1930s. It examined priests James Robinson, Samuel Penney and John Tolkien. Robinson was moved to another parish after complaints in the 1980s without police being told, then fled to the US in 1985 while still receiving archdiocesan support; he was later extradited and jailed for 21 years.
cases.cite: IICSA, Archdiocese of Birmingham Investigation Report, 20 June 2019

cases.n: Deetman Commission — Catholic Church in the Netherlands
cases.victims_note: 'Several tens of thousands' of children had unwanted sexual contact with church officials (survey estimate; other coverage cites 10,000–20,000)
cases.who: Catholic dioceses and religious orders in the Netherlands
cases.cover: Policy of 'not hanging out the dirty washing'; bishops and officials knew and did not act
cases.d: The commission led by former minister Wim Deetman, set up by the church in March 2010, reported on 16 December 2011. It identified at least 800 priests, monks and other religious who abused children between 1945 and 1985, 105 of them still alive, and estimated tens of thousands of victims. It found bishops and officials knew of the abuse and followed a policy of avoiding scandal.
cases.cite: Commissie-Deetman, 'Seksueel misbruik van minderjarigen in de Rooms-Katholieke Kerk', 16 December 2011, as reported by DutchNews.nl

cases.n: Adriaenssens commission and Vangheluwe resignation, Belgium
cases.victims_note: 475 complaints in the first half of 2010; 13 suicides reported
cases.who: Catholic Church in Belgium, about 29 religious orders; Bishop Roger Vangheluwe of Bruges
cases.cover: Judicial raid in June 2010 seized the commission's files (later ruled disproportionate); commission members resigned
cases.d: Bishop Roger Vangheluwe of Bruges resigned in April 2010 after admitting he abused his nephew from 1973 to 1986. The church-backed commission led by psychiatrist Peter Adriaenssens received 475 complaints in six months; its report of 10 September 2010 recorded 13 suicides linked to clerical abuse and 102 verified alleged abusers in about 29 orders. In June 2010 police raided church premises and seized the commission's files (Operation Chalice/Kelk); an appeals court later ruled the raids disproportionate.
cases.cite: Commission for the Treatment of Complaints of Sexual Abuse in a Pastoral Relationship (Adriaenssens report), 10 September 2010, as reported by RTÉ

cases.n: MHG study — German Bishops' Conference
cases.who: German Catholic dioceses
cases.cover: Researchers found personnel files had been destroyed or manipulated
cases.d: The study by researchers from Mannheim, Heidelberg and Giessen, commissioned by the German Bishops' Conference and presented on 25 September 2018, found 1,670 clerics (4.4% of clergy) accused of abusing 3,677 minors between 1946 and 2014. The authors called the figures conservative and found that personnel files had been destroyed or manipulated.
cases.cite: MHG study, 'Sexueller Missbrauch an Minderjährigen durch katholische Priester, Diakone und männliche Ordensangehörige', 25 September 2018, as reported by JURIST
